overview.headline: Bubble sort by adjacent swaps and repeated passes

keyPoints.point: Students learn how comparing adjacent items and swapping items orders a list through passes.
keyPoints.quote: comparing each adjacent pair of items in a list in turn, swapping the items if necessary

keyPoints.point: Students learn that repeating a pass through the list continues until no swaps remain.
keyPoints.quote: repeating the pass through the list until no swaps are done.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that arbitrary data affects runtime and that approaches for nearly ordered lists differ.
keyPoints.quote: Complexity is O(n^2) for arbitrary data, but approaches Θ(n) if the list is nearly in order at the beginning.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that a pass moved an item into its final place and can decrement the last checked position.
keyPoints.quote: Since at least one item is moved into its final place for each pass, an improvement is to decrement the last position checked on each pass.

keyTerms.gloss: Repeated adjacent comparison sort that restores order

keyTerms.quote: Also known as sinking sort, exchange sort.
